column1: # Hand-checked segmentations, used as a regression set for the segmenter.
# Deliberately NOT derived from `word_decompositions`: that table is itself
# produced by running `segment()` over the sources' example words, so scoring
# against it would only measure the segmenter's agreement with itself.
# Lines beginning with GAP are words this pass is known NOT to handle, kept
# here so the reason stays recorded and so a future pass can measure progress.
# Their stated cause is in the trailing comment.
# Native Germanic stems are absent from both sources, which are Greek/Latin
# root dictionaries. No algorithm change reaches these; they need a free-stem
# These need BOTH a free stem and an allomorphy rule, and the stem is the
# binding constraint: `believe`, `happy` and `admit` are all absent from the
# morpheme table, so an allomorphy layer alone closes none of them. Measured
# over a 4000-word sample, only 2.6% of failures are even candidates for
# allomorph rescue, and most of those are false positives (`airport` -> root
# `aire`, `genius` -> root `geny`). Do the free-stem list first.
